newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico seeks tequila recognition in Asia, Africa.
newsitem.headline: Mexico seeks tequila recognition in Asia, Africa.

text.p: Mexico, recognized as the official home of tequila in Europe, will try to win a similar status in Asia and Africa, an industry leader said late on Wednesday.

In February, Mexico won denomination of origin protection for tequila and its cousin mezcal in the European Union. This means those exotic spirits, which are made from cactus plants, may be marketed in Europe only if they are produced in Mexico.

"We will look to achieve similar results in Africa and Asia ... where we expect in the short term to win recognition of our tequila," Carlos Orendain Hernandez, president of the Chamber of the Tequila Industry, told reporters.

Once considered a crude firewater, tequila has gained popularity in Europe in recent years as a fine spirit that can cost more than $100 a bottle. Mexicans usually drink it in a shot glass at room temperature but it is also the ingredient that gives a kick to margaritas and other cocktails.

Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, in the city of Tequila to present an annual award for the cultivation of the agave plant used to make tequila, pledged to support the campaign, saying, "we will continue working to achieve similar agreements in other places."

The Mexican negotiator in the European Union talks, Jorge Camacho, told reporters Mexico would seek official recognition as the home of tequila from Japan. "We have started the first talks with Japan ... and hope that the first meetings can be held in July," Camacho said.
